newsitem.title: USA: Score Board faces "going concern" opinion.
newsitem.headline: Score Board faces "going concern" opinion.

text.p: Score Board Inc on Monday said its auditors planned to include a so-called "going concern" statement in the company's 1996 annual report because of its 1996 loss and weak balance sheet.

In an annual report, auditors issue a "going concern" statement when they have doubts that a company can continue to operate in its present form. The auditors cited a decline in Score Board's working capital and that its liabilities exceed total assets, it said.
Also, Score Board expects a first-quarter operating loss for the first quarter ended March 31.

Score Board, a maker of baseball cards and other entertainment-related memorabilia, said it entered a distribution agreement with Frontier Communications International relating to development and marketing of telephone calling cards.

Also, the company is cutting costs to rectify the company's finances, Score Board said. It said it could not forecast the results of those actions, but the steps were appropriate and would help improve its finances.
